question: Should this bounded performance cache be accepted after current-merge lifecycle proof, given that native cached statements make every future database-owner disposal path responsible for clear-before-close?
rationale: The implementation has a deliberate lifecycle cost that is not resolved by ordinary unit success alone; accepting that ownership invariant is a maintainer risk decision.

options.title: Require current-merge lifecycle proof
options.body: Rebase or test the merge result and confirm the shared and agent database owners still clear cached statements before every close-like transition.

options.title: Accept the documented invariant
options.body: Merge with the current owner audit and focused regression coverage, while treating future cache-enabled database owners as required clear-before-close participants.

recommendation.title: Require current-merge lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Rebase or test the merge result and confirm the shared and agent database owners still clear cached statements before every close-like transition.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the lifecycle audit and authored the latest follow-up fixes affecting the review and proof path.
